name: Squirting — A Distinct Wet Release
summary: Squirting is a unique wet release, distinct from orgasm, that many women experience. It's real and more common than assumed—41% have experienced it, and many spent years thinking they couldn't before discovering they could with understanding and practice.

There's no single magic method; techniques vary widely. The reliable signal is that the path to squirting first produces a weird, unfamiliar feeling—tension, queasiness, or a need-to-pee sensation—which is the green light to continue rather than stop.

6. Take time across sessions to build familiarity—don't expect it immediately.
